# ⚡ Kubernetes Command of the Day (2026-08-24)

## 📌 Watch Pod Status Changes in Real Time

```bash
kubectl get pods -w
```

| Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Category** | `Productivity` |
| **Difficulty** | `Beginner` |
| **Safety Rating** | **🟢 Safe** |
| **Verification Status** | Verified ✅ (Verified on local Kubernetes v1.30 environment.) |

---

### 📖 What It Does

Streams live state transitions, readiness updates, and restart counts for pods in the target namespace.

### 💡 Why It Is Useful

Eliminates repetitive polling or manual terminal refreshes during rollouts, updates, or pod restarts.

### 💻 Practical Example

```bash
kubectl get pods -n default -w
```

### Command Breakdown

- `-w / --watch`: Stream ongoing state modifications after outputting current resource listing.
- `-n / --namespace`: Specify target namespace (defaults to current namespace context if omitted).

### ⚙️ Prerequisites

Requires active `kubectl` connection and appropriate cluster permissions.

### ⚠️ Common Mistake

Running against the wrong namespace or context without checking current-context first.
